categories.name: Simple Weapons
categories.description: Simple weapons require little specialized training and are commonly available.

categories.name: Martial Weapons
notes: Anti-Armored X checks for the Armored Trait tag, not a target's Armor Save characteristic (see Unit Tags).
The Rapier's increased cost reflects its unconditional Critical 1, which converts one failed Hit die after rerolls even without a Surge. As always, Critical Hits bypass Armor/Evade but allow Ward.

categories.name: Heavy Melee Weapons
notes: Heavy weapons follow the normal Heavy restrictions. A Heavy Attack cannot normally be used if the Unit voluntarily Moved or performed a Movement Action during the previous Movement Phase.
Abilities explicitly overriding Heavy restrictions take precedence.

designNotes: v4 balance pass (post-playtesting): Damage-1 weapons gained +1 Attack; Damage-2/Heavy weapons kept their listed Attacks and gained a thematic Anti-[Type] 1 (or, where one already existed, it increased to Anti-[Type] 2, as on the Warhammer), matching the equivalent policy applied to Generic Units.

v5 balance pass (second damage-output pass): Damage-1 weapons gained a further +1 Attack; Damage-2/Heavy weapons raised their Anti-[Type] to 2, except the Warhammer, which already had Anti-Armored 2 and gained +1 Attack instead. The Mace now costs 15 Points.
